record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: For the weakly singular Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (V_αu)(t) + (V_{θ,α}u)(t) with 0 < α < 1, if u_h \in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) is the collocation solution and u_h^{it} is the associated iterated collocation solution, does one have the graded-mesh estimate \|u-u_h^{it}\|_\infty \le C_m(r)N^{-(m+1-α)} on meshes t_n=(n/N)^rT whenever r \ge m/(1-α)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2 Let the given functions g, K0, K1 in the VFIE (3.4) have continuous derivatives of order m+ 1, let b(t) \equiv 0, and assume that the delay function θ is subject to conditions (N1)–(N3) with d = m + 1 in (N3). If uit h is the iterated collocation solution corresponding to the collocation solution uh \in S(−1) m−1(Ih) for (3.4), and if the collocation points are as in Conjecture 3.1, then for graded meshes of the form Ih := {tn = (n/N) rT (0 \le n \le N)}, with r = r(α) \ge m/(1 − α), we have \|u − uit h \|∞ \le Cm(r)N −(m+1−α).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the weakly singular Volterra functional integral equation
  u(t) = b(t) u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (V_α u)(t) + (V_{θ,α} u)(t),  t ∈ I := [0,T],
where 0 < α < 1, the operators are defined by
  (V_α u)(t) = ∫_0^t (t-s)^{-α} K_0(t,s) u(s) ds,
  (V_{θ,α} u)(t) = ∫_0^{θ(t)} (t-s)^{-α} K_1(t,s) u(s) ds,
and θ : I → I is a vanishing-delay function (θ(0)=0, 0 ≤ θ(t) < t for t∈(0,T], θ continuous and strictly increasing). Assume that g, K_0, K_1 possess continuous derivatives up to order m+1, that b(t) ≡ 0, and that θ satisfies the standard smoothness conditions ensuring that the exact solution u has the typical singular behaviour at t = 0 induced by the weakly singular kernel and that θ^{(j)}(0) for 1 ≤ j ≤ m+1 are compatible with the integration scheme.

On the graded mesh
  I_h := { t_n = (n/N)^r T : 0 ≤ n ≤ N },
with grading exponent r = r(α) ≥ m/(1-α), let u_h ∈ S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) (the space of piecewise polynomials of degree ≤ m-1 with no global continuity imposed) be the collocation solution determined by collocation at the points t_{n,i} = t_n + c_i h_{n+1} (1 ≤ i ≤ m) using a fixed set of collocation parameters 0 < c_1 < … < c_m ≤ 1 (assumed chosen as in the standard superconvergence theory). Let u_h^{it} denote the corresponding iterated collocation solution.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant C_m(r), independent of N, such that
  ‖u − u_h^{it}‖_∞ ≤ C_m(r) N^{-(m+1-α)}.

artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals active research on collocation and iterated collocation for delay Volterra integral equations with weakly singular kernels on graded/quasi-graded meshes, including superconvergence results for related vanishing-delay problems. However, no source was found that explicitly establishes the conjectured global error bound C_m(r) N^{-(m+1-α)} for the iterated collocation solution in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) for the full weakly singular VFIE with vanishing delay under the grading r ≥ m/(1-α). The current status of this specific conjecture could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Convergence analysis of collocation solutions for delay Volterra integral equations with weakly singular kernels
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence analysis on uniform and graded meshes for delay Volterra integral equations with weakly singular kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Related convergence results exist for delay weakly singular VIEs on graded meshes, but not for the exact iterated-collocation conjecture stated.

status_evidence.title: Theoretical and numerical analysis of a first-kind linear Volterra functional integral equation with weakly singular kernel and vanishing delay
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a first-kind weakly singular VFIE with vanishing delay, analyzing numerical methods.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses VFIEs with vanishing delay and weakly singular kernels but does not state a proof of the specific iterated-collocation bound.

status_evidence.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Lists conjectures and open problems regarding collocation and iterated collocation for VFIEs with vanishing delays.
status_evidence.claim: The estimate is posed as a conjecture in the survey on open problems for VFIEs with vanishing delays.
